report.summary: Chunk 18 of 25: apply_attempt_memory function that sinks candidates based on history, with detailed docstring and logic.
risks: line 2041 | medium | Function apply_attempt_memory: docstring claims 'A PENALTY, not a filter' but code modifies offset and may sink candidates; if offset < cand.offset, sunk++ but candidate still in out list, so not filtered. However, if offset >= cand.offset, held++ but candidate still in out list with possibly same offset. So it's a reordering, not a filter. Claim is kept. | Check that no candidate is ever removed from the list; code shows all candidates appended to out.

line 2041 | medium | Docstring: 'HOW FAR it sinks is OUTCOME_POLICY's decision, not a constant' - OUTCOME_POLICY is not defined in this chunk, verdict uncheckable. | Verify OUTCOME_POLICY exists and behaves as described.

line 2041 | medium | Docstring: 'outcome is applied as a CEILING on the measured offset, so the score itself distinguishes...' - code uses ceiling from policy.ceiling(same) and clamps offset. But the score is set to SOURCE_BANDS[cand.source] + offset, which may not reflect the ceiling if offset was already below ceiling. Claim is kept. | Check that score calculation uses the clamped offset.
line 2041 | medium | Comment: 'LINEAGE matched, DEFINITION did not' - lineage is not defined in this chunk; refers to task_id matching. Claim is uncheckable.

line 2041 | medium | Comment: 'The audit trail for the number above: the ceiling, what it was applied to, and the argument for that ceiling' - code adds evidence fields like memory_outcome_residual, etc. Claim is kept.
line 2041 | medium | Comment: 'so a human reading the review packet can re-derive the score and refuse the policy' - review packet not defined in chunk, uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Implement apply_attempt_memory to sink candidates based on history.

symbols.name: apply_attempt_memory
symbols.note: Takes candidates and history, returns tuple of candidates and notes. Modifies evidence and score of candidates based on prior attempts.

claims.text: Sink candidates the ledger has already seen attempted, and say so.
claims.why: Function returns a tuple of candidates (sunk ones remain) and notes describing what happened. It sinks by adjusting offset and score.

claims.text: A PENALTY, not a filter. Dropping attempted work would let one transient runner failure delete a real task from the queue forever, and would let the queue silently empty -- both worse than showing the work with its history attached.
claims.why: All candidates are appended to out list; none are removed. Sunk candidates have their offset reduced, but they remain in the output.

claims.text: The operator (and ``--once``) still sees every candidate; what changes is the order, and every moved candidate carries the evidence that moved it.
claims.why: All candidates are in out list. Evidence dict is updated with memory-related fields. Order is affected by score changes.

claims.text: HOW FAR it sinks is :data:`OUTCOME_POLICY`'s decision, not a constant: the outcome is applied as a CEILING on the measured offset, so the score itself distinguishes 'a patch is waiting for you' from 'the gates said no' from 'the worktree would not build'.
claims.why: OUTCOME_POLICY is not defined or imported in this chunk. The code uses outcome_policy(matched.get('last_outcome')) and policy.ceiling(same), but the implementation of outcome_policy is not present.

claims.text: Before this, all three sank identically and the difference survived only in the reason text.
claims.why: Refers to previous behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: LINEAGE matched, DEFINITION did not: the id is stable across definition changes, so this is genuinely different work wearing a familiar name. Record the lineage, do not sink it -- penalising it would be evidence about a task nobody is proposing any more.
claims.where: comment within if not same block
claims.why: The code increments redefined counters and appends candidate with evidence['memory'] explaining it is not treated as already attempted. It does not sink it.

claims.text: The audit trail for the number above: the ceiling, what it was applied to, and the argument for that ceiling -- so a human reading the review packet can re-derive the score and refuse the policy, not just the sort.
claims.why: Code adds evidence fields: memory_outcome_residual, memory_outcome_severity, memory_offset_ceiling, memory_offset_before, memory_policy. These provide the audit trail.

observations.what: Function uses _clamp and BAND_SPAN which are not defined in this chunk; may be imported or defined elsewhere.
Function uses SOURCE_BANDS and replace which are not defined in this chunk; likely imported.
Function uses _candidate_definition_fingerprint which is not defined in this chunk; likely a helper function.
The docstring mentions OUTCOME_POLICY but the function uses a local function outcome_policy; there may be a module-level constant or import.

The evidence field 'prior_attempts_same_definition' is set to same, but 'prior_attempts_same_instruction' is also set to same; they are always equal in this code. This may be a bug if they should differ.

The function returns notes as a list but the return type is tuple[tuple[Candidate, ...], tuple[str, ...]]. The code at the end appends to notes but the final return statement is missing in this chunk (ends with 'if not notes:').
